teams.heading: Fiji, winless in five, face an Italy side beaten twice this month
teams.body: Saturday's Round 6 test takes Fiji to the Bluenergy Stadium in Udine, where Italy close out their run of three November home matches in the Nations Championship. The Azzurri have lost both so far, 7-66 to South Africa in Turin and 14-19 to Argentina in Genoa. Fiji head coach Jake White's side go into the weekend bottom of the log, winless in five, after a 15-43 defeat by Ireland. Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada names his team on Thursday.

lead.why: Only new Fiji men's 15s item: it confirms the Udine venue and Italy's two November defeats ahead of Fiji's next test.

teams.heading: England's next opponents New Zealand beaten 35-28 by Wales in Cardiff
teams.body: Wales centre Eddie James made 25 tackles and scored one of his side's five tries in the win, including a stop that held the All Blacks' Anton Lienert-Brown just short of the line. New Zealand were without Cam Roigard, Damian McKenzie, Will Jordan and Jordie Barrett at the Principality Stadium. Head coach Steve Borthwick's side beat Japan 78-15 in Round 5; of the 194 fans in the app who answered, 93% were buzzing.

lead.why: Fresh coverage of New Zealand's defeat in Cardiff, the main form story about England's next opponents.

teams.heading: Antoine Dupont turns 30 two days after his 'masterclass' against South Africa
teams.body: The France captain hit the milestone on Sunday, two days after the 21-19 defeat of the Springboks at the Stade de France, in which, says Midi Olympique journalist Jérôme Prévôt, he delivered a "masterclass." Prévôt traces his career back to Castres, where Dupont made his professional debut against Leinster in the European Cup on 26 October 2014, aged 17 and needing a dispensation to play against adults. Then-France coach Guy Novès gave him his Test debut in Italy during the 2017 Six Nations.

lead.why: A fresh milestone for the France captain straight after his standout display against the Springboks. The Alldritt return was already reported today.

teams.heading: Dan Sheehan to return to full training as Jamie Osborne ruled out
teams.body: Centre Osborne's pectoral injury, sustained early against Fiji, is one of three fresh Ireland casualties. Debutant replacement No. 8 James McNabney is unavailable while on a 12-day return-to-play protocol, and replacement tighthead Sam Illo enters the concussion process. Hooker Sheehan, named captain for this month's matches, missed that 43-15 win after a concussion against Argentina but is in line to face South Africa on Saturday. Fans in the app were happy with the Fiji result: of the 42 who answered, 69% were buzzing.

teams.heading: Fernandez says Italy create chances but lack finishing before Fiji test
teams.body: Italy breakdown coach German Fernandez remains confident in the squad despite defeats by South Africa and Argentina, saying Italy keep creating chances but lack finishing — and that the players have the quality to fix it. Reviewing the 14-19 loss in Genoa, he noted Argentina were down to 13 men after two yellow cards and said Italy had no truly easy penalty kicks. Ahead of Saturday's Fiji test, he warned against losing attacking ball to a side that thrives in chaos.

lead.why: It is the freshest Italy story: a coach's verdict on the Argentina defeat and his plan for Fiji, not covered in earlier editions.

teams.heading: Planet Rugby ranks 'most accomplished' Finn Russell among world's top 10 fly-halves
teams.body: Planet Rugby's November list of the world's best No. 10s bills Scotland fly-half Finn Russell as 'most accomplished', though it places a rival it labels the 'greatest player' above him. The verdict follows a mixed afternoon for Russell in Sunday's 15-12 win over Australia at Murrayfield. He hit the post with an early conversion and was beaten in the tackle for Harry Potter's first-half try. He then landed the 75th-minute penalty that gave Scotland breathing space before Saturday's meeting with Japan.

lead.why: It is the only new Scotland item, and it centres on Finn Russell; the match, defence and match-ball stories have already run.

teams.heading: Eddie James calls Wales' All Blacks win 'best day of my life'
teams.body: Wales centre James, 24, made 25 tackles and scored one of Wales' five tries in Saturday's 35-28 win over New Zealand, admitting afterwards he could barely feel his feet. His tackle stopping Anton Lienert-Brown just short of the line was among the defining moments. With only 55,152 at the Principality Stadium, he wants the win to draw more supporters for Australia's visit: "The more fans we have, the louder it is." Of 139 fans in the app who answered after full-time, 99% were buzzing.

lead.why: A fresh Wales post-match reaction from a standout performer that has not been covered in a previous edition.

teams.heading: Midi Olympique warns Pumas must raise game to avoid Paris thrashing
teams.body: Midi Olympique journalist Jérôme Prévôt was unimpressed by last weekend's 19-14 win over Italy in Genoa. He called it a narrow victory over a truly mediocre Italian side and a disappointing rough draft that Argentina must improve on against France in Paris to avoid a thrashing. He noted that the penalty count finished 16-16 and that the Pumas trailed until the 38th minute. Italy fly-half Paolo Garbisi then kicked a late penalty dead with the hosts still able to win.

lead.why: It is the only new Argentina item, a pointed French verdict on the Italy win ahead of the France test.

teams.heading: Les Kiss sees 'every chance' of Wallabies improvement before home World Cup
teams.body: Grilled in Edinburgh on whether time remains before next October's home World Cup in Perth, Wallabies head coach Les Kiss said he was happy with it. "I do think there's every chance that there will be improvement," he said after Sunday's 12-15 loss to Scotland, a fourth straight defeat. Next is an attack reboot before Wales in Cardiff, after the Wallabies' lowest points total in 15 Tests; captain Harry Wilson conceded it "probably didn't get to where we would have liked to be."

lead.why: A fresh Kiss response on the World Cup timeline and an attack reboot before Wales. The sevens item falls outside the men's 15s brief.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones' 'play the house down' vow ends in 13-try Twickenham hiding
teams.body: Japan head coach Eddie Jones promised before last Saturday's Nations Championship match against England that his side would "play the house down." What followed at Allianz Stadium was a 15-78 defeat in which England ran in 13 tries, five of them by England's Will Joseph. Writing for the Guardian, Gerard Meagher said the Brave Blossoms "looked like Sunday afternoon amateurs." The loss leaves Japan tenth of 12 in the log with one win from five going into the Round 6 meeting with Scotland.

lead.why: Most-corroborated Japan story not yet run here: Jones' pre-match vow set against what followed.

teams.heading: Rennie says All Blacks 'let the country down' as Tupaea faces surgery
teams.body: Outside centre Quinn Tupaea, a fixture in the All Blacks' side throughout 2026, needs surgery on a thumb injury and will miss the next 10 weeks, ruling him out of Saturday's test against England at Twickenham. Head coach Dave Rennie, demanding a reaction after the 35-28 loss to Wales, said of his players: "They know we let ourselves down and we let the country down." Rennie is set to recall a host of big names, and star wing Will Jordan is in the selection mix after a hamstring problem.

lead.why: Fresh New Zealand news before England: an injury to a regular starter and Rennie's own verdict on the Wales loss.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus asks if unpunished knee-drops in France defeat amount to match-fixing
teams.body: Speaking in Dublin on Monday, Springbok head coach Rassie Erasmus claimed 17 knee-drop tackles went unpenalised in Friday's 19-21 defeat by France. "If he saw it and decided not to act on it, is that not match-fixing?" he asked of the TMO, before insisting it was not an accusation. He also predicted Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast, cited for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji, would escape a ban on a technicality for Saturday's test. Of the 43 fans in the app who answered after the France result, 63% were fuming.

lead.why: Erasmus raising match-fixing over unpunished tackles is the fresh South Africa event every fan is talking about before Dublin.
